One, there is the problem is password shucking
https://www.scottbrady91.com/authentication/beware-of-password-shucking#:~:text=Password%20shucking%20is%20a%20method,it%20to%20its%20weaker%20algorithm.

Two, prehashing is not as simple as it looks.  From https://security.stackexchange.com/questions/61595/is-it-good-practice-to-sha512-passwords-prior-to-passing-them-to-bcrypt

_You still want to exercise caution about some practical details. In particular, many bcrypt implementations expect a password, i.e. a sequence of characters, terminating with the first byte of value 0x00. The output of SHA-512 is binary and thus may contain some bytes of value 0x00. For instance, 1/256th of all passwords will yield a hash value which begins with a byte of value 0x00, that a string-based bcrypt instance will understand as equivalent to an empty password._

Three, the canonical implementations of bcrypt silently truncate after 72 bytes https://passlib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/lib/passlib.hash.bcrypt.html
